label: human-15
people: [gecko]thebluegecko (34), Cortex from B5 (the start script listed his team as Armada; his units were Cortex); computer_whisperer (the user) hosting as a spectator, silent in the chat
our_side: three Armada seats on the east strip: t1 G1 (ai 0), t3 G4 (ai 2), t2 H8 (ai 1); one Opus 5.5 player at effort medium for all three seats, no commander; hands Jev jev-latest (jev-1.13.0), hands effort normal; the standing brief docs/briefs/player.md; realtime lobby game
summary: A realtime 3v1 on Comet Catcher: one Opus 5.5 player on three Armada seats against thebluegecko (Cortex, B5). It ended at 10:20, when a Stout and Shellshocker push killed his commander at B4; his plant fell at 10:21. Our side out-expanded him from the start (18 extractors at 4:11 and 47 at 9:13, against at most 13 of his seen) and lost only two extractors, both to two Rascals at 2:57 and 3:21. Its army led by 3.5x or more from 4:11 (6.3k against about 0.5k seen at 7:30), but until 7:30 the packet kept it off his plant and commander and sent Blitz groups one at a time to D4 and C4. There his Incisors (17 Blitzes killed, 4:00-7:00) and then Pounders (16 Blitzes and 5 Stouts, 6:00-10:00) won the exchanges, and the seen trade stood at 3,964 lost to 2,941 destroyed at 8:12. The player moved two plants to Stouts at 6:02 and the third at 8:12, sent one heavy body at his plant at 7:30, and the push was fighting at his base from 9:37; his commander killed 16 of ours before it died, and he never showed tier 2 or fought in our half after 3:00.

root.what: Nothing ever put the win at risk; this root marks where the game's cost and length were set (the reader's reading, no person commented). With the side's army at about 3.5x his seen, the packet sent each Blitz group to spot_33 (D4) to join one body that raided outer spots, and repeated that it never goes at his plant or commander (first said at 2:37, again at 6:02). Blitzes walked in a few at a time to his Incisors and then Pounders until the 7:30 push order; that one body ended the game in under three minutes.

our_mistakes.what: The lead was kept off the kill. From 4:11 to 7:30 the side's army was 3.5x to over 12x his seen, yet the packet sent it to raid outer spots and barred his plant and commander. One body sent at his plant by about 5:00 would likely have ended the game minutes earlier and saved the Blitzes lost to Incisors and Pounders. This is the reader's reading, backed by thebluegecko's 'time to go fight and win' (L-lead-use-it).
our_mistakes.evidence: 2:37, 4:32 and 6:02 instructs: 'never goes at his plant at spot_36 or his commander'; minutes.py t1 WINDOWS '5:00-10:00 (2.3-17.3x, 6 min)'; one body from E3 at 8:46 to his commander's death at 10:20

their_play: thebluegecko played Cortex from B5, with a single vehicle plant standing at B4 by 2:20 and a construction turret beside it by about 9:00. He raided our south seat early, with two Rascals that killed two fresh extractors at 2:57 and 3:21, and otherwise defended his half with light turrets on his extractors (one killed a Rover at 2:57) and Exploiters on outer spots (by 5:39). His army changed as ours did: Incisors from about 4:00, which killed 17 Blitzes in C4/B3/D4 by 7:00; Pounders from 5:40, which killed 16 Blitzes and 5 Stouts; a Brute by 7:54. He fought only in his own half (his mass C4/B4, 0% in ours after minute 3) and showed no tier 2. At the end his commander fought at the plant and killed 16 of ours before dying at 10:20. His extractors seen never passed 13, against our 47. A 3v1 at even resources with his economy unseen: the reader cannot say how far behind he was, only that he held a negative trade against us until the base fell.

bears_on.note: He brought Pounders in from 5:40, which killed 16 Blitzes and 5 Stouts. Our switch to Stouts (medium tanks), last plant at 8:12, carried the push that killed him. The player's own summary: 'Blitzes lost the trade to Pounders 6:30-8:30'.
Our Blitz mass was answered first by Incisors (17 Blitzes killed) and then by Pounders, while our plants kept making Blitzes.
The side led 3.5x to over 12x in army from 4:11, and the lead went into raids until the 7:30 order to push. One body then went from E3 at 8:46 to his commander's death at 10:20.
Blitz groups reached D4 one at a time from 4:32, and at 7:54-8:04 the hands split three hunts ahead of the body. The trade was negative until the base fell.
The 9:45 order was to attack his commander first when seen, and it died at 10:20, but only after it had killed 16 of ours at its plant.
The first Rovers were in his half at 2:07 and found his base, but killed nothing. The first kills (an extractor, a constructor and an Incisor at B3) came with the Blitzes at 4:19.
The Rovers got within 281 of his start at 2:31 without doing damage (trade 0 destroyed at 3:06), and one died to a light turret at 2:57.
Plants were idle 13-14% of their time on uncounted produce entries, by the player's own note and the records' idle flag.
The side held 47 extractors at 9:13 against at most 13 of his seen and lost only two. The economy carried a negative army trade through to the win.
Wreck fields at C4 and B3 reached 4,259 metal and were never worked, in a game short enough that it did not matter.
Every seat built three solars and then a constructor as the plant's first unit (1:24), as the lesson intends, but the plants stood at 1:23-1:33, past the pool's p75.
There were 8 wakes on blocked plant exit lanes, and t1 lost 430 unit-seconds to stuck units.

bears_on.id: Going and the lead: a lead decays, one body from a gathering place, arrive together, the ball's return home, only the army wins
bears_on.note: A gathering place at D4 in his units' reach, filled one group at a time, fed the trade. The single heavy body, once committed at 7:30, closed the game in under three minutes, inside the pool's 3.4-minute median from twice the army to the end.

bears_on.id: Unit matchups and mixes: counters, the Blitz and the Stout, splash and spacing, body size
bears_on.note: 33 Blitzes died to Incisors and Pounders (17 and 16), the seen trade stood at 3,964 lost to 2,941 destroyed at 8:12, and the Stouts won the base. It is the vehicle twin of 'Blitzes die to line bots; Stouts from the first one seen'.

bears_on.id: Ahead on the trade and lost: the 3v1 pattern
bears_on.note: This game is the converse: behind on the seen trade from about 6:30 to 10:14 (8,471 lost to 6,891 at 10:14), and won on extractors and a commander kill. It bounds the trade as a measure; the premise that a game is decided by the commander or the economy holds.

bears_on.note: Two Rascals took seat t2's two new extractors at 2:57 and 3:21 with no answer and no turret. The south picket was ordered only at 4:32.

bears_on.id: Energy in the opening: solars before and with the plant, the metal-bound first four minutes, the solar rule, the commander on the plant
bears_on.note: Three solars came before the plant, which started at 1:04-1:14, factory units by 4:00 fell below p25, and the energy store was empty for 19.6-22.5% of the game on two seats.

lens.caveats: No ledger row exists for human-15 and no review.md. No person commented on the game: the chat holds only 'gl hf' and 'wp!', the user was silent, and the player's closing question went unanswered. The per-match tools read record-0 only, so seats t2 and t3 were read through scratchpad views with record-1 and record-2 (and their jev logs) renamed. There is no truth file: his army, extractors and economy are what we saw (floors), and pro_baseline's pressure rows are blank. pro_baseline needed --all-starts because G1, H8 and G4 are not carded starts. The root is the reader's reading of a won game. The only word from the user dated 'during human-15' (design 2026-10-03, one brief with everything in it) is about the brief, not this game.

open_questions: What would thebluegecko have done differently against the three seats? Our player asked at 10:29 and the chat holds no answer; did he answer the user elsewhere?

The player's note says groups' 'march' held the push back. hands_window shows group_G_t1 walking back to spot_37 at 8:27 after meeting four units at C3, then shelling from 8:41. Was that the march rule or the hands' retreat rule?
Were the exit-lane blockers (constructors and the commander, 8 wakes) building in the lane (the 2026-10-13 fix) or stuck?
Why did no constructor take apart the wreck fields after the 6:02 and 7:30 orders: were their lists never empty, or was the reclaim option never offered?
